title: Field journal: quantization quality vs economics sweep (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working field journal capturing a mixed workload sweep comparing quality and economics tradeoffs across INT8, FP8, GPTQ, and AWQ quantization backends. We focused on: (1) token-level quality regressions on representative evals, (2) p50/p95/p99 latency behavior under bursty client mixes, (3) kernel-level jitter and tiling interactions with batching and KV cache, and (4) cost-per-1k-tokens estimates for production routing decisions.

Summary (top-level):
- INT8: best steady-state throughput and lowest average cost. Observed p99 spikes caused by kernel tiling contention for certain sequence lengths and attention sizes. Quality regressions are concentrated in rare-token generation (low-prob tail) and early prompt sync points.
- FP8: highest fidelity vs FP32 baseline on perplexity and EM-like QA checks, but ~10-18% higher per-token latency in our stacked kernels (warm steady-state). Tail latency better behaved in some kernels due to denser FP compute paths. Cost is higher than INT8 but lower than full FP32.
- GPTQ (post-training quant): good compromise for static models with minimal quality drift on static evals, but fragile under dynamic-length prompts with long KV cache reuse (sequence-skip artifacts).
- AWQ (adaptive weight quant): best quality for attention-critical layers when run selectively, but introduces more microburst jitter due to mixed-kernel orchestration and memory layout changes.

Experimental setup:
- Models: LLaMA2-13B (baseline), Falcon-7B, and a lightweight 6B test model for stress probes.
- Backends: INT8 (custom packing + tiled GEMM kernel v3), FP8 (E4M3 style emulation path), GPTQ (8-bit weight table), AWQ (per-layer adaptive pack).
- Hardware: p4d-style GPU cluster equivalent (A100), and a consumer class A6000 for profile parity. All runs pinned to single GPU instance; multi-GPU orchestration is out of scope for this sweep.
- Workloads: 60/40 split doc-generation (long: 1024 tokens) vs chat-turns (short: 64-128 tokens). Burst profile: Poisson arrivals with mean rate tuned to 80% of p50 throughput. Client sim produced 10k requests per run.
- Metrics captured: tokens/sec (throughput), latency p50/p95/p99 (ms), perplexity on WikiText-103 subset, QA-em exact-match on a 500-example in-house devset, token-deletion/regression rate (fraction of tokens that differ from FP32 top-1 after quantization), and cost/1k-tokens (estimated infra cost delta).

Key runs and numbers (representative):
- LLaMA2-13B, long-docs:
  * INT8: throughput 18.6k tok/s, p50 34 ms, p95 89 ms, p99 220 ms, perplexity +6.4% vs FP32, QA-EM delta -2.8 points, cost per 1k tokens baseline = $0.62.
  * FP8: throughput 15.5k tok/s, p50 40 ms, p95 92 ms, p99 160 ms, perplexity +1.2%, QA-EM delta -0.5 points, cost per 1k tokens = $0.78.
  * GPTQ: throughput 17.3k tok/s, p50 36 ms, p95 95 ms, p99 205 ms, perplexity +2.7%, QA-EM delta -1.1 points, cost/1k = $0.68.
  * AWQ (layer-hybrid: attention FP8, rest INT8): throughput 16.1k tok/s, p50 38 ms, p95 90 ms, p99 175 ms, perplexity +0.9%, QA-EM delta -0.4 points, cost/1k = $0.72.
- Short-chat workload (mix):
  * INT8 shows best avg latency p50 but p99 spikes up to 1.8–2.5x during microburst windows when tiled GEMM enters a high-contention path for particular batch shapes.
  * FP8 exhibits more stable p99 but higher p50 consistently.

Observed failure modes / oddities:
1) Kernel tiling resonance: For sequences that are multiples of 128 tokens, tiled GEMM kernel used on INT8 path sometimes runs into cache-associativity contention, producing ~2–3x CPU->GPU launch jitter in 0.5% of requests; manifests as p99 spikes. Reproducible on both A100 and A6000 with same kernel binary.
2) Attention-head scale noise (AWQ): AWQ selectively quantizing attention projection weights reduces systematic bias but introduces per-token amplitude jitter that slightly shifts top-1 in rare-token contexts. Cumulative effect shows up on multi-turn QA chains with anchored ground-truth.
3) KV re-use artifacts (GPTQ): GPTQ's static packing reduces code path diversity but when KV-cache is reused across many short turns, we see sequence-skip artifacts where token probabilities drift after 6+ rewrites of cached keys. Likely related to small FP accumulative error in mixed-precision matmuls.
4) Prefetch/kv-cache interplay: When prefix caching is enabled aggressively, INT8 path benefits most in throughput, but interactions with the tiled kernel scheduler increase jitter at p95 since some batches bypass the fast-path and hit the slow-path with prefetch stalls.

Microprofiling highlights (kernels):
- Tiled GEMM v3 (INT8): highest throughput per-core, but sensitive to micro-batch shape and L2 associativity. Active fixer: add a fast-path lane for common (1, n) batch shapes.
- Vector-lane GEMM (FP8): slightly lower peak throughput but deterministic latency across shapes; fewer cold-cache launch penalties.
- Mixed-kernel orchestrator (AWQ+INT8): orchestration overhead ~1.5–2 ms per call when switching kernel flavor within the same request. This hits short-chat latency disproportionately.

Qualitative quality checks:
- Perplexity moves correlate with QA-EM delta but not perfectly; some templates degrade perplexity by +0.5% yet produce -3 points EM loss (sensitive token positions).
- Token-deletion/regression metric is useful to flag catastrophic token shifts for customer prompts; INT8 had 0.24% token-reg rate on our 10k sample dev prompts, AWQ hybrid 0.09%, FP8 0.06%.

Routing and policy implications:
- Default: route low-SLA, cost-sensitive customers to INT8 with automated canary probation (traffic shadowing) for 48 hours before full rollout.
- Mid-tier: GPTQ for predictable throughput + moderate fidelity; enable KV-consistency checks for chat-heavy customers.
- High-SLA: FP8 or AWQ hybrid with reserved capacity to avoid kernel switching jitter; present customers with estimated cost delta and flag for opt-in.

Immediate action items (short):
- (Aisha) Add a microbenchmark to exercise tiled GEMM at 128-token multiples with 50k iterations and collect L2 cache evict traces. (Due: 2025-11-10)
- (Miguel) Prototype a kernel-prefetch fast-path that inspects batch shape and routes to vector-lane GEMM for _small_ microbatches; measure overhead. (Due: 2025-11-17)
- (Jin) Build a lightweight token-regression alert in console that surfaces prompt templates with >0.5% token-reg in canary traffic. (Due: 2025-11-20)
- (Lina) Draft customer-facing note describing FP8 benefits and expected cost delta; coordinate with Solutions Eng for rollout. (Due: 2025-11-24)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we reduce AWQ orchestration penalty by fusing kernels for attention+ffn when AWQ is enabled on contiguous layers? Risk: increased memory pressure.
- Is the tiled GEMM p99 jitter purely hardware cache associativity or are there allocator/pathological memory access patterns in our packer? Need full hw counters.
- How do mixed-tenant workloads on Dedicated nodes amplify these effects? Plan: run a multi-tenant replay with production traces.

Notes on reproducibility and artifacts:
- All harnesses live in GITHUB-PR-2213. Microbench configs are under /bench/harnesses/quant-econ-sweep-v2.
- Confluence planning doc: CONFLUENCE-Quant-Econ-Plan contains the original sweep matrix and cost model assumptions.
- Raw traces (kernel timelines + perf counters) are archived in the internal blob store; index keys attached in JIRA-SERV-879.

Short heuristics for rollout (one-liners):
- If customer p50 requirement <= 50ms and cost-sensitivity high -> INT8 canary + shadow FP8 for quality monitoring.
- If customer demands EM-like fidelity for QA pipelines -> prefer FP8 or AWQ-hybrid on reserved capacity.
- For chat-heavy with long KV reuse -> prefer GPTQ with KV-consistency probes enabled.

Appendix (quick logs excerpt):
- 2025-11-05 03:12 UTC: observed tiling spike co-located with background eviction task on node 12; p99 went from 210ms to 760ms for 0.3% of requests.
- 2025-11-07 10:45 UTC: AWQ canary reduced QA-EM delta from -2.8 to -0.6 on subset A, but p50 increased ~12ms.

Concluding notes:
This sweep suggests there is no one-size-fits-all quantization policy. INT8 yields the best economics but requires mitigations for rare p99 pathology. FP8/AWQ improve fidelity and reduce token-regression but at a cost and with orchestration complexity. Next step: implement the kernel-shape fast-path and the token-regression dashboard to make canaries safer and faster to evaluate.

Unresolved: handoffs to SRE for L2 associativity traces and to Release for canary gating policy.

End of journal entry.
